title: Review: Le Chatelier and industrial compromise; Kc calculations and Q; Oxidation states and half-equations
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AQA A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: EQ02#t4 term and clue written for the game; RX01#t1 term and clue written for the game; RX01#t4 term and clue written for the game; EQ02#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: EQ02#N.14, EQ03#N.8, RX01#N.11a, EQ02#N.12, EQ03#N.6a, RX01#N.14, EQ02#N.7a, EQ03#N.14a, RX01#N.6a, EQ02#N.5, EQ02#N.3a. The matching task revisits terms from the worlds it reviews, in a new mix. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Equilibrium constant
items.clue: The value K, which only a change in temperature can alter.

items.label: Redox
items.clue: A reaction in which loss and gain of electrons happen together.

items.label: Reduction
items.clue: Gain of electrons, as when each O atom goes from 0 to −2 during rusting.

items.label: Le Chatelier's principle
items.clue: When a system at equilibrium is disturbed, it shifts so as to partly oppose the change.

questions.stem: Methanol is made from CO(g) + 2H₂(g) ⇌ CH₃OH(g). The forward reaction is exothermic. Plants run it at high pressure. Why does raising the pressure, by reducing the volume, increase the equilibrium yield of methanol?

options.text: K increases at high pressure, so more methanol is present at equilibrium.
The forward reaction is exothermic, so high pressure pushes the position right.
The position shifts right: the right side has fewer moles of gas.
More frequent collisions at high pressure speed up the forward reaction only.

questions.explanation: 3 mol of gas on the left, 1 on the right. Raising the pressure favours the side with fewer gas molecules, which partly opposes the change.

questions.stem: 0.400 mol SO₂ and 0.200 mol O₂ are sealed in a 2.00 dm³ vessel. At equilibrium the vessel contains 0.300 mol SO₃. What is Kc for 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g)?

options.text: 360 dm³ mol⁻¹
180 dm³ mol⁻¹
360 mol dm⁻³
120 dm³ mol⁻¹

questions.stem: In acidic solution, MnO₄⁻(aq) is reduced to Mn²⁺(aq) and Fe²⁺(aq) is oxidised to Fe³⁺(aq). In the balanced overall redox equation, what amount of Fe²⁺ reacts with 1 mol of MnO₄⁻?

options.text: 1 mol
5 mol
2 mol
3 mol

questions.explanation: Mn goes from +7 to +2, so each MnO₄⁻ gains 5 electrons; each Fe²⁺ loses 1. The iron half-equation is multiplied by 5.

questions.stem: Percentage of NH₃ in the equilibrium mixture at 200 atm (illustrative values): 350 °C, 57% · 450 °C, 36% · 550 °C, 22%. Why do ammonia plants run at about 450 °C rather than 350 °C?

options.text: Because 450 °C gives a higher equilibrium yield than 350 °C.
Because at 350 °C the reaction is too slow; at 450 °C the yield is lower, but far more NH₃ is made per hour.
Because K for this reaction increases with temperature.
Because the reaction is endothermic, so it needs heat to go.

questions.explanation: A compromise: a lower equilibrium yield, reached much faster, gives a higher rate of production.

questions.stem: N₂O₄(g) ⇌ 2NO₂(g). N₂O₄ is placed in a sealed vessel at an initial concentration of 0.200 mol dm⁻³ and the mixture is allowed to reach equilibrium at constant temperature. At equilibrium, [NO₂] = 0.080 mol dm⁻³. What is the value of Kc at this temperature?

options.text: 0.053 mol dm⁻³
0.040 mol dm⁻³
0.032 mol dm⁻³
0.500 mol dm⁻³

questions.explanation: 0.080 of NO₂ uses 0.040 of N₂O₄, so [N₂O₄] = 0.160 mol dm⁻³. Kc = 0.080² ÷ 0.160 = 0.040 mol dm⁻³.

questions.stem: In the thermite reaction, aluminium reacts with iron(III) oxide: Fe₂O₃(s) + 2Al(s) → Al₂O₃(s) + 2Fe(l). What happens to the iron?

options.text: It loses electrons: iron is always oxidised when it reacts, as it does in rusting.
It gains electrons: its oxidation number falls from +3 to 0, and aluminium supplies them.
It loses electrons to aluminium, since aluminium gains the oxygen during the reaction.
It gains electrons: its oxidation number falls from +6 to 0, as Fe₂O₃ has two Fe atoms.

questions.stem: The forward reaction in the following equilibrium is exothermic: 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g). The temperature of the equilibrium mixture is increased at constant pressure. How do the amount of SO₃ and the value of K at the new equilibrium compare with those at the original equilibrium?

options.text: A larger amount of SO₃ and a larger value of K.
A smaller amount of SO₃ and a smaller value of K.
An unchanged amount of SO₃ and an unchanged K.
A smaller amount of SO₃ and the same value of K.

questions.explanation: Raising the temperature favours the endothermic direction, here backward, so there is less SO₃. For an exothermic forward reaction K decreases.

questions.stem: Back to the sealed flask: H₂(g) + I₂(g) ⇌ 2HI(g). It was filled with 0.500 mol H₂ and 0.500 mol I₂ and no HI, in a 2.00 dm³ flask. It has now reached equilibrium and holds 0.800 mol HI. What is Kc at this temperature?

options.text: 2.6 (no units)
64 (no units)
160 dm³ mol⁻¹
0.016 (no units)

questions.explanation: 0.800 mol HI uses 0.400 mol each of H₂ and I₂, leaving 0.100 mol each. Kc = 0.800² ÷ (0.100 × 0.100) = 64. Two terms on top, two below: the volume and the units cancel.

questions.stem: Chlorine reacts with aqueous iron(II) ions: 2Fe²⁺(aq) + Cl₂(aq) → 2Fe³⁺(aq) + 2Cl⁻(aq). Which species is the oxidising agent in this reaction?

options.text: Fe²⁺, since it loses electrons and so is itself oxidised
Cl₂, since it gains electrons and so is itself reduced
Cl⁻, since it is the species holding the gained electrons
None, since no species here gains or loses any oxygen atoms

questions.explanation: Chlorine's oxidation number falls from 0 to −1: each Cl₂ gains two electrons from Fe²⁺. The species that accepts electrons is the oxidising agent.

questions.stem: CH₄(g) + H₂O(g) ⇌ CO(g) + 3H₂(g). The pressure is increased, by reducing the volume, at constant temperature. What happens?

options.text: The position shifts right, giving more H₂; K is unchanged.
The position shifts left, giving less H₂; K decreases.
There is no shift, because every species is a gas.
The position shifts left, giving less H₂; K is unchanged.

questions.explanation: 2 mol of gas on the left, 4 on the right. Higher pressure favours the side with fewer moles of gas, the left. Temperature is constant, so K is unchanged.

questions.stem: The following system is at equilibrium in a sealed container: H₂(g) + I₂(g) ⇌ 2HI(g). More hydrogen is injected, and the temperature and volume are kept constant. Which statement about the new equilibrium mixture, compared with the original one, is correct?

options.text: K has a larger value than in the original mixture.
[H₂] has returned to exactly its original value.
[I₂] is lower than in the original mixture.
[HI] is the same as in the original mixture.

questions.explanation: The added H₂ causes net forward reaction, which uses up I₂ as well as H₂ and forms HI. K is unchanged because the temperature is unchanged.
